purpose: Small controlled evidence-retrieval diagnostic over real algorithm-repository history. It does not score generated answers, patch correctness, actual agent completion time, or real-user conversations.

selection.method: Four explicitly listed genuine fix chains, selected by the AI research agent from official commit metadata before any candidate scores; retain all five AI-authored questions per chain without replacement. This is not a random sample, human-written query set, untouched public benchmark, or evidence of training-data novelty.

source_policy.material: Exact UTF-8 bytes of every changed Python source/test file at the listed first parent and fix, with repository, path, commit, commit author/committer timestamps, Git blob/content hashes and the upstream BSD-3-Clause notice. Other changed files are recorded in provenance and retained where present; no synthetic developer statements or model summaries are substituted.
source_policy.transport: Deterministically chunk original text at at most 900 Unicode characters, prefer the last newline before the limit, zero overlap. Every block retains original start/end character offsets and line range. A source-document transport wrapper is not a real conversation.
source_policy.availability: For every public cutoff, keep only source records with committer time <= cutoff and verified ancestor-or-identical source commit within the same repository. Repeated versions remain separate dated artifacts. Every arm receives the same eligible source blocks and metadata; project selection and cutoff are public task inputs, not hidden answer labels.
source_policy.base_nonleakage: A historical-base query cannot receive its fix snapshot, fix diff/message, future tests, or later-source bytes. Post-fix replay corpora must never be reused as the input history for a future pre-fix code-repair task.
source_policy.verification: Validate the UTF-8 bytes against the upstream GitHub Contents API Git blob SHA at the exact commit/path, then record SHA256, source-span offsets, timestamp order and official ancestry receipts before any retrieval; candidate scoring must not run if a pin, license or count is missing.
source_policy.external_controls: Repository/cutoff/ancestor selection is a shared external harness control with the same public inputs and eligible documents for every arm. It is not native MemoryBook as-of, branch-inference, or automatic repository-selection functionality. The pilot does not credit the product for this filtering.

arms.boundary: Independent SQLite FTS5 BM25 over the same blocks and source metadata. Both documents and queries include literal words plus deterministic underscore/camel/acronym identifier pieces; OR terms, no gold-aware expansion, bm25 then stable source ID. All candidates remain visible; no answer-conditioned fallback.
Published MemoryBook Python API, cache disabled; source bound to exact published runtime.
Frozen candidate MemoryBook Python API, same source blocks/metadata and public controls.

Shared-source component using the unchanged locked BillionKernel default ranker, Node transport, identical project/time availability. Source setup must succeed before the unique claimed matrix; no algorithm modifications.
Empty context diagnostic, no retrieval request or fabricated timing. It is not a generated-answer abstention score.

competitor.license: MIT text plus Additional Term: Attribution on Product Surfaces

controls.readback: Retain native responses and identify the returned original source blocks without gold access. Read each unique native-selected original block, at most five, with no replacement for duplicates or unmapped hits. These common source reads and subsequent packing are recorded separately from native search.
controls.packing: Same original whole source block and same repository/commit/path/line citation header for every arm. Rank-order first fit under each token budget; do not shorten code or add a fact from an unreturned block. Both budget projections reuse the one original retrieval response.
controls.scope: This compares common evidence projections after explicit source-block readback, not native context equivalence or whole-product speed.

evidence: Complete required evidence per answerable question
First required-evidence rank and reciprocal rank
Stale-only and stale-before-current observations where a stale source is defined
Nonempty unsupported retrieval, explicitly not a hallucination or answer-correctness rate
costs: Native kernel time and transport time when available
Explicit source-block readback and common packing milliseconds
Actual packed-context and native-payload reference-token counts
Source ingestion/engine setup milliseconds and persistent state bytes
Worker peak RSS if available, labeled as including evaluator/data and excluding unmeasured child usage
metrics.reporting: All 20 questions, both budgets, every arm, all quality losses and cost increases remain saved. Tiny sequential component timings are descriptive and cannot establish faster AI replies.

scoring.gold_boundary: AI-authored gold span annotations are stored separately and loaded only for saved-output scoring; they are not source documents, query expansions or rank inputs. Original code/tests/commit history are genuine upstream bytes; questions and labels are authored by the research agent.
scoring.decision: Integrity only. No universal candidate acceptance or recall-speed threshold; root's separate registered identifier candidate policy is not silently transferred here.
scoring.small_sample: Four historical chains and authored questions are a bounded pilot, not longitudinal real-user validation or independent evidence for broad generalization.

sequence: Commit this protocol and the exact 20 questions/source pool.
Materialize pinned source bytes, licenses, ancestry proofs and separate gold spans; verify without retrieval or upstream test execution.
Freeze all input/evaluator hashes and source commits in a new binding after their separate Git checkpoint.
Create one immutable source-pair/protocol claim, save fsynced intent/completion events and atomic report checkpoints.
Execute the unique complete registered matrix only after root authorization, retain all errors/unknown outcomes, and independently audit saved results.

future_agent_layer.contract: Separate registered pre-fix sandbox, real model and actual captured tool transcripts; execute hidden FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS guards with all attempts/tokens/time counted. This replay cannot substitute for that experiment.
future_agent_layer.special_environment_note: sympy-finitefield-integer changes the optional python-flint branch; a future repair oracle must install a pinned flint backend and establish base failure. No pure-Python false-positive repair credit.
